chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father used to say: 'Whoever performs Tawaf around this House (the Kaaba) for seven circuits, and prays two Rak'ahs on whichever side of the Masjid he desires, Allah will write for him six thousand good deeds, erase from him six thousand sins, raise for him six thousand levels, and fulfill for him six thousand needs. So whatever of these is hastened, it is by the Mercy of Allah, and whatever is delayed, it is out of Desire to listen to his supplication.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for performing Tawaf and two Rak'ahs of prayer at the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific numerical rewards of six thousand for each spiritual benefit highlight the immense virtue of combining circumambulation with prayer, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence as a means of comprehensive spiritual purification. The distinction between hastened rewards through divine mercy and delayed ones due to longing for supplication reflects the Shia theological understanding of God's responsiveness to the believer's persistent engagement and emotional connection during worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al yamani, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Myasws fatherasws was saying: ‘The one who performs Tawaaf by this House (Kaaba), seven (circuits), and Prays two Cycles in whichever side of the Masjid he so desires to, Allahazwj would Write for him six thousand good deeds, and Delete from him six thousand sins, and Raise for him six thousand Levels, and Fulfil for him six thousand needs. So whatever is Hastened from these, so it is by the Mercy of Allahazwj, and whatever is Delayed from these, so it is out of Desire (of Allahazwj) to Listen to his supplication’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yemaniy from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

my father would say, ‘For one who performs Tawaf around this House seven times and performs two Rak‘at salat (prayer), anywhere in the Masjid al- Haram (the Sacred Masjid), Allah writes for him six thousand good deeds. He deletes six thousand of his sinful deeds, raises for him six thousand degrees and makes his six thousand wishes to come true, of which those earlier are due to Allah’s kindness and those delayed are due to the desire to listen to his prayers.’”
